concept.name: Delta footprint
concept.definition: A footprint display mode in which each price level inside a bar shows the volume delta at that level — ask-traded volume minus bid-traded volume — rather than the raw bid and ask numbers. It highlights where net aggressive buying or selling was concentrated within the bar.
concept.intuition: Instead of showing both sides' scores, it shows only who won each price level and by how much.
concept.mechanics: Per-level delta is computed from classified tick data and displayed as signed numbers (green for positive, red for negative, by convention), with optional background intensity proportional to the magnitude; bar-level totals aggregate the per-level values.
concept.formula: Per-level delta = V_ask(level) − V_bid(level); bar delta = sum over levels
concept.failure_modes: Collapses two-sided information into one signed number, so heavy two-sided trade and light one-sided trade can produce identical deltas; inherits all trade-classification data risks.
concept.misconceptions: A large positive delta cell is not a buy signal — if price cannot advance on that aggression it evidences absorption by passive sellers, which many traders read as bearish.
concept.example: Inside a down bar, one level near the low prints delta +900 while price stalls; the trader notes aggressive buying being absorbed at the low and watches for a reversal or continuation break.
